title: Normalize Product Codes
description:
Acme’s merchandising feed has the right products, but the SKUs are a mess — mixed case, stray spaces, underscores, and double hyphens. Downstream joins against the catalog fail unless every code is normalized the same way.

Normalize `product_code` on every row and write the result as Parquet with overwrite. Keep every other column unchanged; only replace `product_code` (do not add a second code column).

Apply these rules in order: (1) trim leading/trailing whitespace, (2) uppercase, (3) replace any run of spaces, underscores, or hyphens with a single hyphen `-`, (4) drop any character that is not `A–Z`, `0–9`, or `-`.

Input columns: `product_id`, `product_code`, `product_name`. Implement with Spark DataFrame / `pyspark.sql.functions` APIs (`trim`, `upper`, `regexp_replace`, `withColumn`) — no Python loops over collected rows. **Run** uses two smoke testcases; **Submit** uses the full set and row-diffs your Parquet against each case’s `expected/`.

Write results with `df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(OUTPUT_PATH)`. `OUTPUT_PATH` is set by the platform for **this Run/Submit only**.

problemStatement.overview: Normalize product_code (trim → upper → collapse separators → strip junk) and write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH.
symptoms: Catalog joins miss rows because SKUs differ only by case or separators.
Merchandising codes arrive with spaces, underscores, and stray punctuation.
yourTaskSteps: Read input Parquet from INPUT_PATH (platform stages selected testcase inputs).
Overwrite product_code using the four normalization rules in order.
Preserve product_id and product_name; write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH with overwrite.
Submit is graded with a row-level compare against each selected testcase expected/.
problemStatement.yourTask: Implement src/main.py that normalizes product_code and writes Parquet output.
hints: Chain trim → upper → regexp_replace for separators → regexp_replace to keep [A-Z0-9-].
Prefer withColumn("product_code", …) so you overwrite the same field.
A separator pattern like [\\s_-]+ → '-' works after uppercasing.
spark.read.parquet(INPUT_PATH) reads every staged testcase file.

expectedOutput.description: Normalized SKU: trim, upper, collapse [\\s_-]+ to -, drop other chars

gradeChecks: Spark job succeeds on selected Submit testcases
OUTPUT_PATH Parquet readable with product_id, product_code, product_name
Each Submit testcase expected/ matches candidate rows (key + values)
No extra rows beyond the union of selected expected testcases
